subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: What owner and security contract should portable agent bundles use before any implementation touches agent config or workspace import code?
rationale: The request spans core CLI/Gateway APIs, plugin/bundle distribution, config rewrites, workspace file writes, skills, channel bindings, and secret exclusion, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary or trust model.

options.title: Design core bundle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-owned design of the manifest, dry-run, import/export allowlist, overwrite behavior, and security review before coding.

options.title: Route through plugin/ClawHub APIs
options.body: Treat portable agents as a plugin or bundle-style package and open only narrower core/plugin API gaps that external packaging cannot currently solve.

options.title: Defer to manual migration docs
options.body: Leave current workspace/config/skill migration as documented manual steps until stronger demand or a narrower security-reviewed scope appears.

recommendation.title: Design core bundle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-owned design of the manifest, dry-run, import/export allowlist, overwrite behavior, and security review before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is mainly product/security boundary work, and recent history ties this person to adjacent agent CLI/Gateway refactors and repository scope guidance.
